title: Fluid Resuscitation Intake/Output Trend
scenario: A 54-year-old male client is admitted with sepsis and started on isotonic IV fluid resuscitation. Hourly intake and output are recorded to guide therapy.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the flowsheet trend, how should the nurse interpret the client's response to fluid resuscitation?

options.text: The client is responding appropriately; perfusion is improving
The client is developing fluid volume overload
The client is not responding and needs an immediate fluid bolus stopped
The client is showing signs of acute kidney injury

questions.rationale: Rising urine output, climbing MAP, falling heart rate, and a declining lactate together indicate improving perfusion and an appropriate response to resuscitation.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which findings across the flowsheet indicate the resuscitation is effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Urine output increased from 20 to 55 mL/hr
IV intake decreased in the final hour

questions.rationale: Increasing urine output, rising MAP, falling lactate, and a slowing heart rate all reflect restored tissue perfusion and effective fluid resuscitation.
